title: Anil Suhala v. Purvanchal Vidhut Vitrana Nigam Ltd., Varanasi
coram: Ashwani Kumar Mishra, J.; Vipin Chandra Dixit, J.
disposition: Petition consigned to records; mandamus to restore connection refused.
headnote: Clause 8.1(VII) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code applies only to theft by tampering of the meter and the like, not to drawing supply by a separate unauthorized line tapped to the mains so as to bypass metering. Where action under Section 135 of the Electricity Act, 2003 has been taken, mandamus to restore the connection will not issue; the consumer must challenge those proceedings in the appropriate forum.
facts: Anil Suhala sought immediate restoration of connection No. 704025220593, invoking Clause 8.1(VII) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code on the ground that theft procedure had not been followed. Purvanchal Vidhut Vitrana Nigam Ltd., Varanasi, replied that this was not routine meter tampering: the petitioner had tapped a separate cable to the main line so as to bypass the meter. A provisional bill had been issued and action under Section 135 of the Electricity Act, 2003 taken.

holding_units.topic: 8.1(VII) limited to meter-tampering theft, not unauthorized line
holding_units.holding: Clause 8.1(VII) applies only where theft of electricity is on account of tampering of meter etc. It has no applicability where a separate unauthorized line is laid to obtain supply so that consumption is not metered.

holding_units.topic: no mandamus to restore while s.135 action is taken
holding_units.holding: Where the consumer was found drawing supply by a separate cable to the main line, bypassing the meter, and action under Section 135 has been taken, no mandamus can issue to restore the connection. The remedy is to challenge those proceedings in the appropriate forum.

not_decided.point: merits of the s.135 proceedings and the provisional bill
not_decided.note: petitioner left to challenge them in the appropriate forum
